title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

reading.body:
This is a compliance failure at the physical infrastructure layer of a data center build, not a failure inside a model or a decision system. Sixty-two natural gas generators of 2,000 kilowatts each were installed and operated at the Vineland site without permits to be installed or operated. The site was under construction and partly in use, so the equipment was running in a live deployment rather than in a test or staging phase.

Catching this would have required a permitting check at two points: before the generators were installed and before they were energised. The violation was found by state inspectors in late July, not by the operator's own controls, and the resulting penalty was issued under the state's Air Pollution Control Act. The campus is also the subject of noise complaints and violation orders from the Cumberland County Health Department, which are separate from the air pollution finding.

What is not established is whether the operator knew the generators lacked permits, whether the noise complaints and the air pollution violation share a cause, and whether any AI workloads were served by this equipment. The federal lawsuit from homeowners is an allegation, not a finding, and no outcome in it is reported.

reports.title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

summary:
New Jersey fined DataOne $1.07 million on Tuesday after state inspectors found 62 tractor trailer size natural gas generators at its Vineland data center site in late July. None of the 2,000 kilowatt generators had permits to be installed or operated. The fine was for violating the state's Air Pollution Control Act and is the largest ever issued to a New Jersey data center operator, state officials said.

The Vineland campus is under construction and is slated to finish at the end of the year. It is planned as a 2.6 million square foot complex needing 350 megawatts, enough to power a medium size city. Some of it is already in use. It has drawn complaints, including a federal lawsuit from homeowners over persistent noise and violation orders from the Cumberland County Health Department for excessive noise. Governor Mikie Sherrill said data center builders must benefit New Jersey communities.
